paper_summary: LSU MSc thesis (P. Bhat, 2009) on the thermal characterisation of plain and carbon-nanotube reinforced epoxy / 3M S22 glass-microballoon syntactic foams. Foams were cast with 0, 10, 20 and 50 vol% S22 microballoons and 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5 vol% commercial MWCNTs mixed into the resin (NMSF), and compared with a novel nanotube-grown syntactic foam (NGSF) in which 6-20 nm MWCNTs were grown on the microballoon surface by two-stage thermal CVD over an electroless nickel catalyst. Densities and void contents are tabulated for all 16 mixed/plain compositions; laser-flash thermal conductivity increased 86% over plain syntactic foam for NGSF (0.26 vs 0.14 W/m-K near room temperature) while nanotube mixing slightly decreased it (0.13 W/m-K).

extraction_notes: Only thermal/physical data - this thesis reports no mechanical tests, so modulus/strength fields are null throughout. Sixteen records come from Table 7 (theoretical and actual density, kg/m3 -> g/cm^3, and void content % -> fraction, mapped to matrix_porosity_fraction); nanotube loadings for those rows come from Table 6 and the SF/NMSF nomenclature of Sec. 3.1.3. Four of those rows (SF2200-00, NMSF2200-01/-02/-05) contain no microballoons - they are the neat-resin and MWCNT/epoxy baselines from the same table and are recorded with particle_volume_fraction = 0. Thermal conductivity: the full k vs volume-fraction data set exists only as plots (Figs. 33, 34 and 60, with measurement levels labelled 43, 62 and 91 C; Sec. 4.1 describes the nominal set points as 50, 70 and 100 C), and no numbers are printed on those axes, so no values were read off them. The only conductivities stated numerically anywhere in the text are the three in Sec. 5.6 (plain SF 0.14, NMSF 0.13, NGSF 0.26 W/m-K 'close to room temperature'), which are the last three records; test temperature was set to 43 C, the lowest plotted level. The Sec. 5.6 sentence does not say which NMSF nanotube loading nor which of the four NGSF samples the quoted values belong to, hence the lower confidence and the composition ranges kept in sample_label / additional_fillers. The four NGSF compositions of Table 18 (0.77/2.01/2.77/2.82 vol% CNT = 1.61/4.01/5.19/5.65 wt%, all at 50 vol% GMB) carry no printed property values, so they were not split into separate records; their composition is preserved in the NGSF record. test_type is 'other' for every record: laser-flash conductivity and density determination have no dedicated enum value. S22 properties (true density 220 kg/m3 = 0.22 g/cm^3, radius ratio 0.922, 35 um mean outer diameter, 1.26 um wall) are from Table 2 / Sec. 3.1.1.2 and are cited by the thesis from other sources but describe the particles actually used. cure_or_process_temperature_c = 100 C is the 3 h post-cure (initial cure was 36 h at ambient). Values quoted in the Chapter 2 literature review (e.g. single-MWNT k ~2000-3000 W/m-K, aluminium 235 W/m-K) are for non-syntactic-foam materials and were not recorded.
